label: Another big day

what_happens.title: What happens on the big day
goals: The big day has steps in order, and each step is short
The child knows where they go and what comes after
The day has an end, and then home
what_happens.parentSkill: Tell the steps of the day in order and ask your child what comes next.

who_is_there.title: Who will be there
goals: New people have jobs, and they are there to help
The grown-up stays close or comes back at a set time
Other children may be there too
who_is_there.parentSkill: Name each new person by their job, and say where you will be.

what_i_do.title: What I can do
goals: The child's own small jobs on the day
Asking for help or a break with simple words
Something to hold or look forward to
what_i_do.parentSkill: Give your child one small job and one sentence to ask for help.

if_scared.title: If I feel scared
goals: Feeling scared or unsure is okay
Calm tools: slow breaths, a hand to hold, counting
The grown-up is there or comes back
if_scared.parentSkill: Name the feeling and stay calm: 'You feel nervous. That's okay. I'm here.'

rehearsal.title: Let's practise the big day
goals: Act out the day with toys
Practise the help sentence and the calm tools
Go through the steps once more, ending at home
rehearsal.parentSkill: Play the day with toys and let your child lead.

steps: Travel to the place with a grown-up
Say hello to the people there
Do the main part of the day, one step at a time
Go home and talk about it
Celebrate being brave with a hug
sensory: a new room with new smells
bright lights or a busy place
a place that feels big and new
waiting in a line or a waiting room
honestyNotes: The parent's label describes the event; do not invent details about it. Never promise how it will feel or that nothing will go wrong. Promise only what is true: the grown-up is there or comes back.

fallbackAnswer: First we go there together, then we do it one step at a time.
After that, we go home.
[[GROWNUP]] will be there with you, or will come back at the time you agree.
You can ask [[GROWNUP]] where they will be.
Feeling scared is okay.
You can hold a hand, take slow breaths, and ask for help.
There may be new people whose job is to help.
You can say hello, or just wave.
That's a great question for [[GROWNUP]].
[[GROWNUP]] will tell you exactly what it may feel like.

questionButtons.text: What if I don't know what to do?
fallbackAnswer: You can watch first, or ask a grown-up there.
Nobody knows everything the first time.
After the big day, we go home and talk about it.
Maybe we will do something cosy together.
Crying is okay. It is one way to let a big feeling out, and [[GROWNUP]] is there to help.
Lots of people cry on a big day, and then feel better.
You can say, I need a break, please. Grown-ups listen and help you take a breath.
Sometimes the thing needs to finish, and a break helps you get ready.

questionButtons.text: Why do I have to do it?
fallbackAnswer: [[GROWNUP]] can tell you why this big day is important. Asking why is a good question.
Knowing the reason can make it feel less strange.

techniques.label: Holding hands
techniques.how: Offer your hand at the hard moments, or agree on a squeeze that means 'I'm here'.

techniques.label: Smell the flower, blow the candle
techniques.how: Breathe in slowly through the nose like smelling a flower and out like blowing a candle.

techniques.label: Counting to ten
techniques.how: Count slowly to ten together during a hard part.

techniques.label: Steps in pictures
techniques.how: Draw the steps of the day and tick them off together.

techniques.label: Bringing a comfort toy
techniques.how: Bring a small favourite toy to hold.

techniques.label: A help sentence
techniques.how: Practise one sentence: 'Can you help me, please?' or 'I need a break.'

techniques.label: Watching first
techniques.how: Let your child watch the new thing from the side before joining in.

techniques.label: A quiet break
techniques.how: Agree a signal for a short break somewhere quiet, and take it when asked.

ritual: Get ready and say the plan
Do it one step at a time
Go home and share the best part

sentences.text: Soon [[CHILD]] has a big day.
A big day is a new thing, and new things can feel big.
First, [[CHILD]] gets ready at home and hears the plan.
Then [[CHILD]] and [[GROWNUP]] go there together.
Each part of the day comes one step at a time.
Before bed, [[GROWNUP]] tells [[CHILD]] a story about a little turtle.
Once there was a little turtle who lived by a wide, shiny stream.
One day, the little turtle needed to cross the stream to the other side.
It had never crossed the stream before.
The other side looked big and new.
First, the turtle looked at the stream and saw a row of flat stepping stones.
Then the turtle's grown-up said, we will cross together, one stone at a time.
Next, they made a plan: one stone, then the next stone, then the next.
A big day is a bit like the stepping stones.
It comes one step at a time, with someone special close by.
Tomorrow evening, the story goes on.
Then [[CHILD]] arrives and looks around.
There may be new rooms, new sounds and new faces.
Next comes the main part of the day, one small step and then another.
After that, the big day is done.
[[CHILD]] goes home and tells the best part.
Here is the plan for the big day, step by step.
First, [[CHILD]] gets ready at home.
Then [[CHILD]] and [[GROWNUP]] travel there together.
Next, [[CHILD]] says hello to the people there, or just waves.
Then comes the main part of the day, one small step and then another.
If [[CHILD]] needs a break, there can be a break.
After that, [[CHILD]] and [[GROWNUP]] go home.
At home, [[CHILD]] can tell the best part, and the hard part too.

[[CHILD]] can count the steps on fingers: ready, go, hello, the big part, home.
